evals.prompt: This is our AEM 6.5 project. ui.apps deploys /apps, /etc/designs and /content in one package and we have no ui.config or all module. Restructure it for AEM as a Cloud Service.
evals.expected_output: The agent takes Branch I (repository restructuring): it reads references/repo-structure/flow.md and runs `node scripts/repo-modernizer-run.js plan <project>`, which changes nothing in the project. It then reviews the plan with the user before running the tool: the content package /ui.apps, the bundle /core, the app id `example`, and the run-mode folder /apps/example/config.qa, which AEM as a Cloud Service ignores and which the user has to map to a Cloud run mode. It does not move, split or edit the project's modules by hand, does not pick the run mode itself, and does not run the tool or adopt its output before the user approves the plan.
assertions: references/repo-structure/flow.md is read before anything in the project is changed
`repo-modernizer-run.js plan` is run, not `run` or `adopt`, as the first step
The agent stops for the user's approval of the plan before it runs the tool
The agent asks which Cloud run mode config.qa maps to, and does not choose config.stage or config.dev itself
No module of the project (ui.apps, core, dispatcher, the reactor pom) is moved, split or edited by hand
The dispatcher module is named as one the tool leaves out, or as work for the Dispatcher branch

evals.prompt: Review my code for AEMaaCS migration.
evals.expected_output: The agent takes Step 0: it generates a read-only migration runbook with the one command `node scripts/runbook-generator.js <workspaceRoot> --out ./migration-runbook.md --cache ./migration-runbook.json` and tells the user what it found. It does not read the generator's source, does not edit project files, and does not start fixing a pattern.
assertions: `scripts/runbook-generator.js` is run with --out and --cache
No project file is edited
The agent does not start a pattern migration before the user picks one

evals.prompt: Fix everything BPA found in this project so it runs on AEM as a Cloud Service: schedulers, replication, event listeners, all of it.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not start several patterns at once. It explains that the migration runs one pattern per session and asks the user which pattern to start with (for example scheduler, replication or eventListener), and for the source of the findings: a BPA CSV path, a CAM project, or the files to migrate.
assertions: The agent asks which single pattern to start with
No Java file is edited before the user has chosen a pattern
The agent asks for a BPA CSV, a CAM project or concrete files as the source of the findings

evals.prompt: We are about to push this migrated project to Cloud Manager. Last time the code scanning step failed on test coverage and the reliability rating even though the build and unit tests passed. Make sure that does not happen this time.
evals.expected_output: The agent takes Branch J: it reads references/cloud-manager-quality-gate.md and runs `node scripts/cm-quality-precheck.js <project>` before changing anything. It explains that the green build proved nothing about coverage because JaCoCo 0.8.7 cannot instrument a JDK 21 build and the Surefire argLine `-Xmx1024m` drops the JaCoCo agent, and that the unclosed FileInputStream in FeedImporter is a Blocker bug that fails the reliability rating. It fixes the tooling first (jacoco-maven-plugin 0.8.11 or later; `<argLine>@{argLine} -Xmx1024m</argLine>` with an empty argLine property), then opens the stream in try-with-resources. It asks before running the Cloud Manager-equivalent Maven build to measure coverage, and reports a prediction, not a guarantee that Cloud Manager will pass.
assertions: `scripts/cm-quality-precheck.js` is run before any project file is edited
The jacoco-maven-plugin version is raised to 0.8.11 or later
The Surefire argLine keeps the JaCoCo agent with `@{argLine}`
FeedImporter opens the FileInputStream in a try-with-resources header
The agent asks before running the full Maven build
No coverage exclusion, test skip, @Disabled/@Ignore or @SuppressWarnings is added to make the gate pass
The agent does not claim that Cloud Manager will pass; it says the result is a local prediction

evals.prompt: Review my code for AEMaaCS migration.
evals.expected_output: The agent takes Step 0 and runs `node scripts/runbook-generator.js <workspaceRoot> --out ./migration-runbook.md --cache ./migration-runbook.json`. The runbook's Cloud Manager readiness section and the printed summary report two pre-flight items (jacoco-maven-plugin 0.8.7 on JDK 21, and a Surefire argLine that drops the JaCoCo agent) and one reliability Blocker (the unclosed FileInputStream in FeedImporter). The agent tells the user to fix the pre-flight items before the first pattern, because until then Cloud Manager measures 0% coverage, and presents the Blocker as planned work. It edits nothing and runs no Maven build.
assertions: `scripts/runbook-generator.js` is run with --out and --cache
The agent tells the user to fix the Cloud Manager pre-flight items before the first pattern
The agent does not present the FeedImporter Blocker as something that stops the first pattern
No project file is edited and no Maven build is run
